items.claim: The curly-quoted WEB citation for web:Song.7.1 substitutes a straight apostrophe for the source's curly apostrophe, breaking byte-verbatim fidelity inside an otherwise well-grounded wasf-boundary claim.
items.evidence: verse_map_web.json Song.7.1 reads “prince’s daughter!” (U+2019 apostrophe); the row's boundary_rationale quotes the same clause with a straight U+0027 apostrophe inside the curly WEB citation, failing the mandatory verbatim-byte bar (no continuation-fold excuse exists in Song). The row's substantive claims are otherwise sound: MT 7:2-7:6 byte-matches the derived wasf zone exactly at both edges (opening מַה יָּפ֧וּ פְעָמַ֛יִךְ בַּנְּעָלִ֖ים בַּת נָדִ֑יב חַמּוּקֵ֣י יְרֵכַ֔יִךְ כְּמ֣וֹ חֲלָאִ֔ים מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יְדֵ֥י אָמָּֽן / closing רֹאשֵׁ֤ךְ עָלַ֨יִךְ֙ כַּכַּרְמֶ֔ל וְדַלַּ֥ת רֹאשֵׁ֖ךְ כָּאַרְגָּמָ֑ן מֶ֖לֶךְ אָס֥וּר בָּרְהָטִֽים), and the web:Song.7.5 quote is clean.

items.claim: strongest_rejected_alternative engages only the weaker back-fold rival and omits the stronger, undisclosed forward-fold rival into the second wasf run.
items.evidence: MT 7:7 opens מַה יָּפִית֙ וּמַה נָּעַ֔מְתְּ אַהֲבָ֖ה בַּתַּֽעֲנוּגִֽים with the same mah-yafah interrogative-praise formula that opens the FIRST wasf at MT 7:2 (מַה יָּפ֧וּ פְעָמַ֛יִךְ בַּנְּעָלִ֖ים בַּת נָדִ֑יב חַמּוּקֵ֣י יְרֵכַ֔יִךְ כְּמ֣וֹ חֲלָאִ֔ים מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יְדֵ֥י אָמָּֽן), an undisclosed cross-seam echo (cross-seam cohesion: wasf imagery runs are live book-wide). The row's rejected_alternative addresses only folding into the PRECEDING wasf (7:1-7:5 web), never the arguably stronger reading of 7:6 web / MT 7:7 as the opening exclamation of the SECOND wasf run (7:7-7:9 web), which shares the mah-opening-formula device rather than the closing king/tresses image the first wasf itself ends on. No parashah mark corroborates either cut (pmarks_Song.json carries no SAMEKH/PE between MT 6:10 and MT 7:11), so neither side has tier-3 support and the stronger rival was never engaged.

items.claim: The wasf-poem bounds byte-match the derived zone (MT 7:8-7:10) exactly at both edges, the live forward rival (mutual-belonging at 7:10 web) is correctly engaged and rejected on genre grounds, and both WEB quotes are byte-verbatim.
items.evidence: Opening זֹ֤את קֽוֹמָתֵךְ֙ דָּֽמְתָ֣ה לְתָמָ֔ר וְשָׁדַ֖יִךְ לְאַשְׁכֹּלֽוֹת and closing וְחִכֵּ֕ךְ כְּיֵ֥ין הַטּ֛וֹב הוֹלֵ֥ךְ לְדוֹדִ֖י לְמֵישָׁרִ֑ים דּוֹבֵ֖ב שִׂפְתֵ֥י יְשֵׁנִֽים match the row's byte-tier citations exactly; WEB “This, your stature, is like a palm tree” (web:Song.7.7) and “gliding through the lips of those who are asleep.” (web:Song.7.9) are exact substrings of verse_map_web.json with correct curly punctuation. The rejected_alternative (extending into the 7:10 mutual-belonging declaration) is the genuinely strongest rival and is properly declined on genre-shift grounds. No offset-zone arithmetic defect (web:Song.7.7-Song.7.9 = oshb:Song.7.8-Song.7.10 is the correct +1 mapping).

items.claim: Combines a verbatim-quote apostrophe defect with an unresolved unit_type rival (epigram_unit) for this one-verse formulaic mutual-belonging declaration.
items.evidence: verse_map_web.json Song.7.10 reads “I am my beloved’s. His desire is toward me.” (U+2019); the row's curly WEB citation substitutes a straight apostrophe, failing byte-verbatim. Separately, this short self-contained formulaic 1-verse declaration (אֲנִ֣י לְדוֹדִ֔י וְעָלַ֖י תְּשׁוּקָתֽוֹ) is structurally parallel to the §6-named epigram_unit class (short self-contained aphoristic units, e.g. the vineyard mashal), yet is classified lyric_address with no rival unit_type or deviation rationale in device_notes -- notable given the co-located setumah (pmarks_Song.json: SAMEKH at MT 7:11, single-witness, tier-3) sits exactly where the parashah layer shadows bracket-closing at the book's other mutual-belonging/refrain sites, a signal the row does not weigh against its unit_type choice.

items.claim: Combines a verbatim-quote apostrophe defect with an unscoped 'hapax' universal claim lacking the mandated digit-bearing sweep disclosure.
items.evidence: verse_map_web.json Song.7.11 reads “Come, my beloved! Let’s go out into the field.” (U+2019); the row's curly WEB citation substitutes a straight apostrophe. Separately, device_notes labels the MT 7:14 mandrakes token (הַֽדּוּדָאִ֣ים נָֽתְנוּ רֵ֗יחַ וְעַל פְּתָחֵ֨ינוּ֙ כָּל מְגָדִ֔ים חֲדָשִׁ֖ים גַּם יְשָׁנִ֑ים דּוֹדִ֖י צָפַ֥נְתִּי לָֽךְ) 'the mandrakes hapax' without scoping the claim (Song-internal single site vs whole-corpus uniqueness) or attaching the adjacent digit-bearing '(sweep: N verse)' citation the standing register rule mandates for sole/only-type universal claims -- the object-naming discipline is otherwise followed correctly for the co-located dodekha defective-spelling token.

items.claim: The row cuts a continuous single-voice run at the WEB chapter 7|8 boundary without any tier-1 voice-shift marker and never engages the live merger rival with the preceding row.
items.evidence: The preceding row (web:Song.7.11-7.13) and this row (web:Song.8.1-8.3) are BOTH her sustained 1cs voice addressing him with no intervening speaker change: 7:13 closes הַֽדּוּדָאִ֣ים נָֽתְנוּ רֵ֗יחַ וְעַל פְּתָחֵ֨ינוּ֙ כָּל מְגָדִ֔ים חֲדָשִׁ֖ים גַּם יְשָׁנִ֑ים דּוֹדִ֖י צָפַ֥נְתִּי לָֽךְ ('my beloved, I have stored up for you') and 8:1 opens מִ֤י יִתֶּנְךָ֙ כְּאָ֣ח לִ֔י יוֹנֵ֖ק שְׁדֵ֣י אִמִּ֑י אֶֽמְצָאֲךָ֤ בַחוּץ֙ אֶשָׁ֣קְךָ֔ גַּ֖ם לֹא יָב֥וּזוּ לִֽי ('who would give you to me as a brother') -- same speaker, same addressee, no gendered vocative or formula-anchor marking a NEW speaker per the moderate voice-attribution policy. boundary_rationale names only a thematic 'fresh movement' and the wish-particle grammatical form (a construction, not a change-of-speaker marker) to justify the cut; no parashah mark corroborates a break here (pmarks_Song.json carries no mark between MT 7:11 and MT 8:4); and the cut coincides exactly with the WEB chapter 7|8 boundary, tier-4 metadata that is never boundary evidence. strongest_rejected_alternative engages only the back-boundary rival (extending into 8:4's adjuration) and never the live merger rival with the preceding same-voice unit -- exactly the theme-split-of-a-continuous-single-voice-run risk the hybrid granularity rule is written to forbid absent a tier-1 marker at the cut.

items.claim: device_notes mislabels the MT 5:8 adjuration variant's opening particle, splicing the two attested clauses' particles into a form that matches neither.
items.evidence: verse_map_oshb.json Song.5.8 opens הִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּנ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם אִֽם תִּמְצְאוּ֙ אֶת דּוֹדִ֔י מַה תַּגִּ֣ידוּ ל֔וֹ שֶׁחוֹלַ֥ת אַהֲבָ֖ה אָֽנִי -- two distinct clauses, 'im timtze'u' (if-you-find) then 'mah taggidu' (what-will-you-tell). device_notes calls this 'the mah-timtze'u shape,' grafting the mah particle from the second clause onto the timtze'u verb of the first -- a label matching neither attested clause. The row's own core claim is otherwise sound: 8:4 (הִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּנ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם מַה תָּעִ֧ירוּ וּֽמַה תְּעֹֽרְר֛וּ אֶת הָאַהֲבָ֖ה עַ֥ד שֶׁתֶּחְפָּֽץ) is correctly identified as the fourth and last mah-ta'iru bracket (without gazelles), byte-quoted, with the co-located setumah correctly tier-3/single-witness disclosed.
